claims.text: The d-band center of a transition metal governs its catalytic activity.
A more favorable d-band-center position leads to higher catalytic activity.
Two transition metals with different d-band-center positions can be compared under otherwise identical reaction conditions to isolate the proposed governing factor.
The d-band-center position influences adsorption and desorption of reactants and products.
Changes in adsorption and desorption caused by the d-band-center position affect catalytic activity.
The metal with the more favorable d-band-center position will have higher catalytic activity than a baseline metal with an unfavorable position.
The hypothesis applies where d-band-center position is the primary factor influencing activity.
Surface structure and reaction conditions may influence the relationship between d-band-center position and catalytic activity.
Similar catalytic activities for metals with significantly different d-band-center positions would falsify the hypothesis when it predicts a large activity difference.
